answer: Pairwise-bounded quadratic funding resists sybils: an agent's matched reward grows with the square of its distinct backers, but any two identities whose support correlates get their mutual match capped, like a willow bent back on itself. Clones paid from one vault share a funding signature and collapse to one discounted voice, while a juniper-sparse graph of independent patrons earns the full bonus. To fake real influence an attacker must recruit N uncorrelated funders each locking separate capital, so cost climbs linearly N-times and the correlation penalty compounds beyond that.
